review_notes: I read the whole file and the Basic.lean API it uses: bimoduleTensorLift, bimoduleTensorTmul_mem, bimoduleTensorLift_tmul and the hbalance/hleft/hright hypotheses. I also checked Coproducts.lean for an existing bilinear tmul helper. The only tmul bilinear map there, tensorBilinear, is private and built differently, so it can't be reused here. The forward and inverse constructions (shiftPair/shiftHom/shiftHom_tmul and unshiftPair/unshiftHom/unshiftHom_tmul) are the same argument written twice with different shift bookkeeping. The final iso proofs (hom_inv_id and inv_hom_id) and the naturality proof are short and not worth factoring. I could not compile anything. The helper below is a sketch whose exact universe and carrier-defeq details may need adjusting, because the source and target objects differ only by definitional carrier equalities.

findings.problem: The forward construction (lines 42–84) and the inverse construction (lines 86–140) are the same argument written twice. Each defines a bilinear map by `m ↦ n ↦ bimoduleTensorTmul … m n`, written out field by field. Each proves hbalance with `bimoduleTensorTmul_balance`, and proves hleft and hright with the same `simp only [..., tmul_smul_bimoduleTensorTmul, ← Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def, one_smul]` script. Each proves the degree condition by shifting `bimoduleTensorTmul_mem` and rewriting an `omega` arithmetic identity, then applies `bimoduleTensorLift` and closes the `_tmul` lemma with `rw [bimoduleTensorLift_tmul …]; rfl`. Only the integer bookkeeping differs: `p - a` versus `p + a`. The two copies of the left/right-action proofs and of the `_tmul` lemma must be kept in sync by hand, and any change to the `bimoduleTensorLift` hypotheses has to be made twice.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one private helper above `shiftPair` that takes source graded bimodules `M₁ N₁`, a target `P` with the same carrier as `bimoduleTensorObj Γ Δ Θ M₂ N₂` for some `M₂ N₂`, and a degree hypothesis. Sketch:

private def tmulLift (M₁ : …) (N₁ : …) (P : …) (f : M₁ →ₗ[k] N₁ →ₗ[k] P) (hf : ∀ m n, f m n = bimoduleTensorTmul Γ Δ Θ M₁ N₁ m n) (hdeg : ∀ {p q m n}, m ∈ M₁.grading.piece p → n ∈ N₁.grading.piece q → f m n ∈ P.grading.piece (p+q)) : bimoduleTensorObj Γ Δ Θ M₁ N₁ ⟶ P

together with `tmulLift_tmul : (tmulLift …).hom (bimoduleTensorTmul … m n) = f m n`.

Proof sketch: build `f` from the tmul bilinear map, rewrite with `hf`, and reuse `bimoduleTensorTmul_balance`, `tmul_smul_bimoduleTensorTmul` and `Algebra.TensorProduct.one_def` once. The `rfl` step becomes `bimoduleTensorLift_tmul`. Alternatively, a single private `tmulBilinear M N : M →ₗ[k] N →ₗ[k] bimoduleTensorObj Γ Δ Θ M N` could replace both hand-written structures, and the shift would be applied by composing with the carrier-identity map.

Then `shiftHom := tmulLift … (shiftPair …) rfl (shiftPair_degree …)` and `unshiftHom := tmulLift … (unshiftPair …) rfl (unshiftPair_degree …)`, with each `_tmul` lemma a one-liner from `tmulLift_tmul`. Only the two degree arithmetic lemmas stay specific to each direction. Both are consequences of `bimoduleTensorTmul_mem` and `mem_shiftObj_piece_iff`, so they could also share a lemma stating that `shiftObj` pieces shift by the integer.
findings.benefit: The balance/left/right action reasoning and the pure-tensor evaluation lemma would appear once instead of twice, and the two directions would differ only by their degree lemmas. This shortens the file by roughly 30–40 lines. Future changes to `bimoduleTensorLift`'s signature would touch one place. A reader could see that the isomorphism is 'the identity on pure tensors' with only the degree arithmetic differing.
